ENERGY CONVERSION 
Any proposed conversion plant to be located upon or within 50 miles of the exterior boundary of the diminished Crow Indian Reservation would require specific approval of the Crow Tribe and the Secretary of the Interior; an environmental impact statement would also be required.
There are presently no plans for an energy conversion plant, but such a possibility should be recognized in that there are sufficient coal reserves available as a future supply for coal conversion. As perviously mentioned a detailed environmental analysis would be required prior to approval.
For purpose of this statement it is assumed that a conversion plant would be constructed on or near the Tracis to utilize 6.5 million tons of coal annually over approximately a 40 year period. This corresponds to a 250 million SCF-per-day coal gasification facility or 2,000 MW of electric power generating capacity. Westmoreland Resources would mine coal for shipment at a rate of 14 million tons annually from the Tracts in addition to that mined for conversion at this rate.
Approximately 2750 construction workers would be needed and long-term employment would be 625 personnel during the operational phase of the plant. The plant could consume as much as 16,000 acre feet of water annually. This water would likely come from Yellowtail Dam or the Yellowstone River via a pipeline constructed for this purpose. Either source would require a pipeline 40 to 50 miles in length. Westmoreland Resources currently holds a contract for 30,000 acre feet from Yellowtail Dam for industrial useage.
The coal mine utilized for coal extraction to supply the conversion plant would be similiar to mining plans as described in previous subsections.
